findings.issue: AddAsync is a second, unguarded door into the state machine. When statusTo is Cancelled, Closed or Archived it does `CorrespondenceStateMachine.EnsureTransition(from, target); row.Status = target;` and saves — it never routes through CorrespondenceService.CancelAsync / CloseAsync / ArchiveAsync. So `FollowUps.AddAsync(id, FollowupKind.Note, null, now, statusTo: CorrespondenceStatus.Cancelled)` cancels a numbered letter with correspondence.cancel_reason left NULL (noteAr is optional and is written only to the followups row), which breaks AGREEMENT item 19 «إلغاء المرقّمة بسبب»; the same path closes an item with close_note NULL and archives one with archived_at NULL (CorrespondenceView.CancelReasonAr/CloseNoteAr/ArchivedAt all come back null, and 0001_initial.sql has no CHECK constraint to catch it). CorrespondenceService.ChangeStatusAsync is careful to route exactly these three targets to their own methods; FollowUpService is not. Existing tests only pass Done / InProgress / AwaitingReply, so nothing is red.
findings.fix: In FollowUpService.AddAsync, before mutating the row, reject the three targets that carry stored fields: `if (statusTo is CorrespondenceStatus.Cancelled or CorrespondenceStatus.Closed or CorrespondenceStatus.Archived) throw new CorrespondenceRefusedException(<new CoreAr string pointing at the dedicated command>);` — or, if the timeline shortcut is wanted, take ICorrespondenceService as a constructor dependency and delegate to CancelAsync(noteAr)/CloseAsync(noteAr)/ArchiveAsync before writing the follow-up entry (those already write the audit row and the status follow-up, so AddAsync must then not write a second one). Add a test asserting that cancelling through AddAsync either is refused or leaves CancelReason non-null, and one asserting ArchivedAt is stamped.

findings.issue: AlreadyImportedAsync matches a stored incoming on `c.ExternalNumber == number && c.PartyNameSnapshot == office` (office = message.SenderOfficeName). But for the internal case of AGREEMENT item 49 — the one the round-trip test sets up, where the recipient's structure does contain the sender's unit — ImportAsync resolves unitId, and CorrespondenceService.SnapshotPartyNameAsync then OVERWRITES PartyNameSnapshot with the LOCAL OrgUnit name at numbering time. The snapshot no longer equals SenderOfficeName, so a second import of the same .wakeel-msg is not recognised: PreviewImportAsync reports AlreadyImportedAr = null (the preview tells the user the file is new) and ImportAsync falls through to the duplicate detector, refusing with «هذا الوارد مسجَّل من قبل بالرقم والجهة نفسيهما» instead of «هذا الملف مسجَّل من قبل». No second number is consumed (the exact-duplicate check still fires on ExternalNumber + UnitId and the draft is discarded), so this is wording plus a false-negative preview, not corruption. It is invisible today only because Importing_the_same_file_twice… (ExchangeServiceTests.cs:136) deliberately omits the AddUnit calls that An_approved_letter_round_trips… (line 32) makes — the two tests exercise different configurations and the gap falls between them.
findings.fix: Resolve the sender unit once per read and match on it: in ImportAsync/ReadAsync compute `senderUnitId = await ResolveSenderUnitAsync(message, ct)` before the already-imported probe, then make AlreadyImportedAsync take it and query `c.Direction == In && c.ExternalNumber == number && c.Status != Cancelled && (senderUnitId != null ? c.UnitId == senderUnitId : c.PartyNameSnapshot == office)`. Add AddUnit(sender office) to the recipient world in Importing_the_same_file_twice_is_recognised_and_then_refused_as_a_duplicate so the internal configuration is the one under test.

findings.issue: ToView derives «متأخرة» with `referral.DueAt is { } due && due < now`, comparing raw DateTimes. Every other service in the package normalises both sides through ArabicRelativeTime.ToUtc (FollowUpService.Card, CorrespondenceService.Validate, the reminder pass). A caller passing a Local-kind `now` — which the screens do, and which ArabicRelativeTime.ToUtc exists to absorb — shifts the overdue boundary by the UTC offset, so a referral can read «مفتوحة» for hours after its deadline or «متأخرة» hours before it.
findings.fix: `var status = referral.Status == ReferralStatus.Open && referral.DueAt is { } due && ArabicRelativeTime.ToUtc(due) < ArabicRelativeTime.ToUtc(now) ? ReferralStatus.Overdue : referral.Status;` and add a theory over a Local-kind `now` on either side of the deadline.

findings.issue: ListAsync applies the free-text filter AFTER `.Take(limit)`: the rows are truncated to the newest `limit` (default 200) and only then normalised and matched. Searching W01 for a subject that sits at position 300 in the newest-first order returns nothing even though the row exists and is not archived, and the result silently looks like «لا توجد نتائج». The in-memory normalisation is the right call (the comment explains why), but it has to run over a window wide enough to answer the question.
findings.fix: When query.Text is non-empty, prefilter in SQL before Take — e.g. `rows = rows.Where(c => EF.Functions.Like(c.Subject, "%"+raw+"%") || EF.Functions.Like(c.OfficialNumber, ...) || ...)` as a cheap net, or read a larger bounded window (say Math.Max(limit, 2000), the same shape DuplicateDetector.SubjectScanLimit uses), normalise-match that, then Take(limit). Add a test that stores limit+50 rows and finds the oldest one by a ة/ى spelling variant.

missing_spec_items: «تذكير عبر ReminderScheduler» for follow-ups is implemented but never invoked: IFollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync has no caller, because ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync (src/Wakeel.Core/Services/ReminderScheduler.cs) is outside this package's allowed paths and is concurrently modified by another agent. A stored follow-up reminder therefore never rings. Correctly reported by the builder; needs assignment to the ReminderScheduler owner or an explicit grant of that file. Everything needed is public (ReminderKeyKind, ReminderKind, CoreAr.CorrFollowupReminderTitle/Body, CorrespondenceService.AuditEntityType).

«حذف المسودة غير المرقّمة نهائيًا» (AGREEMENT item 19) is a soft delete, not a physical one. DATA-MODEL §0 forbids physically deleting a synced row and correspondence carries only AFTER INSERT/UPDATE change_log triggers, so a real DELETE would never propagate and the draft would return on the next sync. User-visible behaviour is identical (global query filter, no restore command). Carried over from round 1; still needs the owner's ratification or a schema change (AFTER DELETE trigger + sync rule) — not fixable inside this package.

DATA-MODEL §0 line 23 still describes correspondence.official_number as an unfiltered global unique index, while Migrations/0003 correctly replaced it with UNIQUE(direction, official_number) — the two independent sequences of ARCHITECTURE §5 legitimately produce the same number text for one incoming and one outgoing letter on the same day. Docs are outside this package's write scope; the schema/docs owner should amend §0.
notes:
Ran exactly `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` (Build succeeded, 0 Warnings, 0 Errors) and `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` (Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 462, Skipped: 0, Total: 462, 23 s). Warnings-as-errors clean; no skipped tests.

Round-1 fixes all verified in place and genuinely fixed, each with a non-tautological test: the CorrectionService two-pass plan/apply (PlannedChange with an Action<CorrespondenceRow> that can only assign — every refusal is raised in pass one, so a half-applied batch can no longer be committed by an unrelated later SaveChanges on the session-lived WakeelDb), DuplicateDetector.SameParty's typed-name arm, ExchangeService's import rollback via DiscardDraftAsync(CancellationToken.None), CorrectionFieldView's Arabic-ready Old/New beside the untouched stored payload, CorrespondenceAr.FieldLabel + CorrFieldUnnamed fallback (no English identifier can reach the user), CorrRefusedCancelDraft, the recipient_only and links_changed audit rows written only on an actual change, the cancelled-export refusal, CorrExchangeSignatureExternal, and the narrowed reminder queries.

What I checked and found sound:
- Numbering: IssueAsync is called only inside BeginTransactionAsync in RegisterIncomingAsync and ApproveOutgoingAsync, both guarded by EnsureUnnumberedDraft, both preceded by EnsureClockAsync so a bad clock refuses in Arabic before a number is touched. RollbackAsync detaches Added entries and reloads the rest, so the tracked official_numbers row cannot keep a rolled-back sequence value and silently skip a number (the AGREEMENT item 37 gap); A_failure_after_the_number_was_issued_rolls_the_number_back_with_everything_else covers it. Migration 0003's per-direction unique index is right — ARCHITECTURE §5's two sequences make the same YYYYMMDD/DESSS text legitimate for one incoming and one outgoing on the same day, and leaving it unfiltered on deleted_at keeps a number consumed forever.
- State machine: the table matches the spec's eight states; Draft leaves only to New (only through registration/approval), Archived is terminal, Cancelled reaches only the archive, same-to-same is refused. CorrespondenceStateMachineTests asserts 14 allowed and 15 refused pairs plus total coverage of the enum and Latin-free wording. Finding 1 above is the one hole in the enforcement, and it is outside CorrespondenceService.
- Duplicates: Jaccard is correct (union seeded from left, intersection counted on distinct right; two empty subjects score 0, not 1) and runs on ArabicText.Normalize'd words split on Arabic punctuation, so «بشأن: الموازنة» and «بشأن الموازنة» agree. Real-Arabic tests cover diacritics, tatweel, ة/ه and ى/ي. A cancelled letter deliberately does not block re-registering the same one, and outgoing is never compared with incoming.
- Exchange: the container is opened twice on purpose — a probe with VerifyCertificateChain=false only to learn the producer's org id, then the real open with the chain verified against the pinned org key when and only when the org matches, which is what lets «التوقيع سليم» be honest and forces «الجهة المرسِلة غير موثّقة لدينا» for item 22. Content key sealed to the recipient's X25519 key with the org recovery copy alongside (item 17); export refuses unapproved and cancelled letters; import refuses a bad signature and a newer formatVersion; every crypto/JSON failure collapses to one Arabic sentence with no error code. Tests cover a package addressed to another device and a tampered file.
- Item 7: the flag is stored, audited on change, and exposed as RecipientOnly/RecipientOnlyAr. AGREEMENT item 7 defines it as «عدم تصدير المراسلة في حزم المزامنة إلا إلى النسخة المستلمة», i.e. enforcement belongs to the sync package builder, not to B3-1 — correct as scoped here, but the sync package owner must read the flag or item 7 stays unenforced end to end.
- Attention/badges: AttentionService already reads New/InProgress/AwaitingReply and maps to CorrespondenceIn/Out; BadgeService groups both under BadgeKeys.Correspondence. The existing attention test uses an overdue InProgress row rather than an overdue AwaitingReply one — same code path, but a test on the awaiting-reply state would close the loop the spec names.
- Arabic: every new string in CoreAr is Arabic with no technical term and no error code; the field-label map means an unknown key degrades to «حقل آخر» rather than an English identifier. One RTL note, not a finding because it matches the established Core convention (AttentionService.cs:42 documents it): composed audit summaries such as CorrAuditCancelled(number, reason) and CorrAuditExported(fileName) embed a Latin/digit run inside an Arabic sentence and are STORED composed, so the screen cannot wrap the run in <bdi> the way it does for a separate number column. If the owner's mixed-direction rule is to hold for the audit log, the isolate (U+2068 … U+2069) has to go into these CoreAr formatters themselves — worth a product decision, applying to the pre-existing Health* strings too, not just to B3.
- No secret, key or password reaches a log, a view model or the database in clear text; DeviceIdentity is only ever passed through, never stored.
- No file outside the package's allowed paths was touched; the many other modified/untracked paths in the tree belong to the concurrent design-system and screen packages and were left alone.
